change: the last three cyber quizzes: five stems reworded, and a fourth markup generation so 3.5 can be lifted
_context: 22 of 25 cyber quiz pages are server-scored. The three left, 2.3, 3.5 and 4.1,
were refused by scripts/extract-cyber-quizzes.js for two different reasons.
Five stems named the CED to a student, which lib/quiz-citation.js refuses.
The rewordings were put to Tanner in docs/cyber-last-three-quizzes-decision.md
and approved. Four are deletions; 4.1 Q6 is a real rewrite because dropping
It would have been half the work to patch a local copy of each body, run the
extractor on that and skip the sheet. That is routing around a guard to get
the output it was refusing, and the result looking identical is what makes it
the wrong habit to leave behind. The seed is GENERATED from live bodies and
--check re-derives it, so the corrected stem has to be live.
3.5 needed no rewording. It needed a fourth markup generation, and a human
call on its ten items sitting inside the 9-to-24 teacher-bundle range.
That confirmation is per page and per COUNT, not a raised ceiling.

checks._why: What was confirmed is an instrument, not a handle. An eleventh question is a changed instrument and a changed decision.

checks.name: X4 the option scope goes greedy and swallows the following options

_withdrawn.name: R4 the stem-scope check is removed, so an edit could land in an explanation
_withdrawn._why: WITHDRAWN because it came back GREEN, and a green mutation run is a failed check rather than a passing one. Assertion 4 in the generator is a TOTAL blast-radius check, undoing the five edits must reproduce the original byte for byte, and it catches any edit landing anywhere it should not. No single-guard mutation gets past it. The scope check is labelled as producing a better error at the right moment rather than as the only defence, and the suite exercises it directly on a body where the text appears once and outside a stem.

_withdrawn.name: R5 4.1 Q6 is 'fixed' by deletion, leaving a broken sentence
_withdrawn._why: WITHDRAWN as a pass/fail, kept as a finding. Replacing the Q6 rewording with a bare deletion, which leaves 'which CIA principle does most directly associate with it', leaves the whole suite green. No automated check can judge whether a rewritten sentence reads like English. That is not a gap to close, it is the reason lib/quiz-citation.js says rewording belongs to a human, demonstrated rather than asserted.
